pk.title: Humyn Labs Raises USD 47M in Series A to Scale Physical AI Research and Deployment
pk.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Humyn Labs, a Physical AI research and deployment company, today announced USD 47 million in Series A funding to accelerate robot deployment-readiness across real-world environments in Brazil, South Korea, and India. Co-Founder Ishank Gupta (L) Co-Founder Manish Agarwal (R) Humyn labs The USD 26 million equity round was led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC, and marquee angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic. The USD 21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital. Humyn Labs has surpassed USD 50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. Working with frontier AI labs, robotics companies, and world-model developers, it runs capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia. The funding will support deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea, and India; capture hardware and enrichment engines; and on-the-ground presence in San Francisco, London, and Seoul. Founded in 2026 by Manish Agarwal (IIM Ahmedabad) and Ishank Gupta (The Wharton School), Humyn Labs turns human experience into physical understanding for robots by capturing real-world work across factories, warehouses, farms, and homes. Its proprietary capture devices record specific jobs to lab requirements, while its data engine converts recordings into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion, and touch. Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs, said, "Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from. This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand globally. With a USD 10 billion opportunity in data infrastructure, we aim to build a USD 1 billion annual revenue business." Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs, said, "A robot does not learn a job from the internet; it learns from the person who has done it for twenty years on the floor. We bring the model lab and site operator onto that floor together so every deployment teaches the next model." Pratik Agarwal, Partner, Accel, said, "Physical AI is a defining technology shift of the next decade, and data and deployment are where the real moat will be built. Humyn Labs has the technical depth and customer pull to be a category leader." Explore careers at humynlabs.ai/careers. Contact: Sharmilee Daru SD@4WDtechPR.com

pk.title: Hisense Makes Everyday Laundry Simpler with Smarter Care
pk.description: QINGDAO, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hisense, a leading brand in global consumer electronics and home appliances, believes technology should fit naturally into everyday life. Its 5i heat pump washer dryer brings this philosophy to the laundry room, combining a standard-size footprint with a larger drum for greater capacity, while fitting seamlessly into existing cabinetry and taking more of the guesswork out of everyday laundry. Hisense 5i Heat Pump Washer Dryer For many people, laundry comes with familiar moments of uncertainty: Will a favorite cashmere jumper lose its shape? Is this fabric safe to tumble dry? Which cycle is right for a mixed load? And where is there room to dry everything? The 5i is designed around these concerns, bringing Gentle Care, Fit&Max capacity, four A-class ratings under the EU energy label, and AI Super Wash & Dry together in one appliance. Its heat-pump drying system maintains a precise 40°C Gentle Dry temperature, significantly lower than conventional condenser models, providing gentler care for fabrics while recycling heat for greater efficiency. With a 12kg wash capacity and 8kg drying capacity, the large drum handles bigger loads while the standard-size design fits naturally into the home. The 5i brings intelligence through AI Super Wash & Dry. Its 13 sensors monitor factors including load weight, water hardness and temperature, automatically adjusting the cycle to suit each load. Its 4A energy efficiency can also help reduce the energy cost of everyday laundry. This thinking extends to Hisense's AI Companion Laundry Suite, introduced at IFA 2026. By recognizing clothing characteristics, the suite automatically selects suitable wash and dry cycles and adjusts the process, accordingly, creating a more seamless load-and-go experience. For Hisense, intelligent technology should work quietly in the background, making everyday routines simpler and giving people more time for the moments that make life brighter. About Hisense Hisense, founded in 1969, is a globally recognized leader in home appliances and consumer electronics with operations in over 180 countries, specializing in delivering high-quality multimedia products, home appliances, and intelligent IT solutions. ae.title: Youdao Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results
ae.description: HANGZHOU, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Youdao, Inc. ("Youdao" or the "Company") (NYSE: DAO), an AI solutions provider specializing in learning and advertising, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Total net revenues were RMB1.4 billion (US$213.1 million), representing a 12.3% decrease from the same period in 2025. - Net revenues from learning services were RMB609.4 million (US$90.9 million), representing a 5.2% decrease from the same period in 2025. - Net revenues from smart devices were RMB145.2 million (US$21.7 million), representing a 40.9% decrease from the same period in 2025. - Net revenues from online marketing services were RMB674.3 million (US$100.6 million), representing an 8.8% decrease from the same period in 2025. Gross margin was 43.6%, compared with 42.2% for the same period in 2025. Income from operations was RMB33.7 million (US$5.0 million), representing a 19.2% increase from the same period in 2025. Basic and diluted net income per American depositary share ("ADS") attributable to ordinary shareholders were RMB0.28 (US$0.04), compared with near zero for the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders were RMB0.38 (US$0.06), compared with RMB0.08 for the same period of 2025. "In the third quarter, we achieved operating profitability for the ninth consecutive quarter, reflecting the continued strength of our business. The strong reception of our newly launched Confucius speech and translation models in the global open-source community further demonstrated our leadership in real-time speech AI," said Dr. Feng Zhou, Chief Executive Officer and Director of Youdao. "Looking ahead, we will continue advancing our AI-Native Strategy, leveraging Confucius LLM to develop compelling products, deepen user engagement, and drive sustainable growth. We remain confident in meeting our full-year financial objectives, with continued improvements in operating profit and cash flow," Dr. Zhou concluded. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Net Revenues Net revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB1.4 billion (US$213.1 million), representing a 12.3% decrease from RMB1.6 billion for the same period of 2025. Net revenues from learning services were RMB609.4 million (US$90.9 million) for the third quarter of 2026, representing a 5.2% decrease from RMB643.1 million for the same period of 2025. Net revenues from smart devices were RMB145.2 million (US$21.7 million) for the third quarter of 2026, representing a 40.9% decrease from RMB245.8 million for the same period of 2025, primarily due to a decline in demand for smart learning devices. Net revenues from online marketing services were RMB674.3 million (US$100.6 million) for the third quarter of 2026, representing an 8.8% decrease from RMB739.7 million for the same period of 2025. The year-over-year decrease reflects Youdao's disciplined, strategic approach to engagement acceptance, which places greater emphasis on higher ROI (return on investment) engagements. Youdao believes this strategy has enhanced the overall operational efficiency of its business. Gross Profit and Gross Margin Gross profit for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB622.7 million (US$92.9 million), representing a 9.5% decrease from RMB687.9 million for the same period of 2025. Gross margin was 43.6% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 42.2% for the same period of 2025. Gross margin for learning services was 59.7% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 58.5% for the same period of 2025. Gross margin for smart devices was 41.0% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 50.3% for the same period of 2025. The decrease was mainly attributable to increased bill-of-materials cost for smart devices. Gross margin for online marketing services was 29.6% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 25.4% for the same period of 2025. The improvement was mainly attributable to improved gross margin profile of performance-based advertisements through third parties' internet properties compared with the same period of last year. Operating Expenses Total operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB589.0 million (US$87.9 million), compared with RMB659.6 million for the same period of last year. Sales and marketing expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB422.2 million (US$63.0 million), representing a decrease of 13.4% from RMB487.7 million for the same period of 2025. This decrease was attributable to the reduced marketing expenditures in smart devices. Research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB118.3 million (US$17.6 million), representing a decrease of 7.4% from RMB127.8 million for the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the decreased headcount for research and development employees, leading to payroll savings. General and administrative expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB48.5 million (US$7.2 million), representing an increase of 10.0% from RMB44.1 million for the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly attributable to an increase in expected credit losses on the Company's accounts receivables. Income from Operations As a result of the foregoing, income from operations for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB33.7 million (US$5.0 million), increasing by 19.2% from RMB28.3 million for the same period in 2025. The margin of income from operations was 2.4%, compared with 1.7% for the same period of last year. Net Income Attributable to Youdao's Ordinary Shareholders Net income attributable to Youdao's ordinary shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB33.4 million (US$5.0 million), compared with RMB0.1 million for the same period of last year. Non-GAAP net income attributable to Youdao's ordinary shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB45.9 million (US$6.8 million), increasing by nearly 4 times from RMB9.2 million for the same period of last year. Basic and diluted net income per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB0.28 (US$0.04), compared with near zero for the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders were RMB0.38 (US$0.06), compared with RMB0.08 for the same period of 2025. Other Information As of September 30, 2026, Youdao's cash, cash equivalents, current and non-current restricted cash, time deposits and short-term investments totaled RMB599.8 million (US$89.5 million), compared with RMB743.2 million as of December 31, 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, net cash used in operating activities was RMB89.0 million (US$13.3 million). Youdao's ability to continue as a going concern is dependent on management's ability to implement an effective business plan amid a changing regulatory environment, generate operating cash flows, and secure external financing for future development. As of September 30, 2026, Youdao has received various forms of financial support from NetEase Group, including, among others, RMB748.0 million in a short-term loan, and US$120.4 million in long-term loans maturing on March 31, 2030, drawn from a US$300.0 million revolving loan facility. As of September 30, 2026, the Company's contract liabilities, which mainly consisted of deferred revenues generated from Youdao's learning services, were RMB771.8 million (US$115.1 million), compared with RMB847.7 million as of December 31, 2025. Share Repurchase Program On November 17, 2022, the Company announced that its Board of Directors had authorized the Company to adopt a share repurchase program in accordance with applicable laws and regulations for up to US$20.0 million of its Class A ordinary shares (including in the form of ADSs) during a period of up to 36 months beginning on November 18, 2022. This amount was subsequently increased to US$40.0 million in August 2023. In November 2025 and August 2026, the Board approved amendments to this Program, each extending its expiration date by one year, ultimately to November 17, 2027. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had repurchased a total of approximately 7.5 million ADSs in the open market under the share repurchase program for a total consideration of approximately US$33.8 million. ae.title: Humyn Labs Raises USD 47M in Series A to Scale Physical AI Research and Deployment
ae.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Humyn Labs, a Physical AI research and deployment company, today announced USD 47 million in Series A funding to accelerate robot deployment-readiness across real-world environments in Brazil, South Korea, and India. Co-Founder Ishank Gupta (L) Co-Founder Manish Agarwal (R) Humyn labs The USD 26 million equity round was led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC, and marquee angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic. The USD 21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital. Humyn Labs has surpassed USD 50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. Working with frontier AI labs, robotics companies, and world-model developers, it runs capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia. The funding will support deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea, and India; capture hardware and enrichment engines; and on-the-ground presence in San Francisco, London, and Seoul. Founded in 2026 by Manish Agarwal (IIM Ahmedabad) and Ishank Gupta (The Wharton School), Humyn Labs turns human experience into physical understanding for robots by capturing real-world work across factories, warehouses, farms, and homes. Its proprietary capture devices record specific jobs to lab requirements, while its data engine converts recordings into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion, and touch. Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs, said, "Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from. This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand globally. With a USD 10 billion opportunity in data infrastructure, we aim to build a USD 1 billion annual revenue business." Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs, said, "A robot does not learn a job from the internet; it learns from the person who has done it for twenty years on the floor. We bring the model lab and site operator onto that floor together so every deployment teaches the next model." Pratik Agarwal, Partner, Accel, said, "Physical AI is a defining technology shift of the next decade, and data and deployment are where the real moat will be built. Humyn Labs has the technical depth and customer pull to be a category leader." Explore careers at humynlabs.ai/careers. Contact: Sharmilee Daru SD@4WDtechPR.com

ae.title: Hisense Makes Everyday Laundry Simpler with Smarter Care
ae.description: QINGDAO, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hisense, a leading brand in global consumer electronics and home appliances, believes technology should fit naturally into everyday life. Its 5i heat pump washer dryer brings this philosophy to the laundry room, combining a standard-size footprint with a larger drum for greater capacity, while fitting seamlessly into existing cabinetry and taking more of the guesswork out of everyday laundry. Hisense 5i Heat Pump Washer Dryer For many people, laundry comes with familiar moments of uncertainty: Will a favorite cashmere jumper lose its shape? Is this fabric safe to tumble dry? Which cycle is right for a mixed load? And where is there room to dry everything? The 5i is designed around these concerns, bringing Gentle Care, Fit&Max capacity, four A-class ratings under the EU energy label, and AI Super Wash & Dry together in one appliance. Its heat-pump drying system maintains a precise 40°C Gentle Dry temperature, significantly lower than conventional condenser models, providing gentler care for fabrics while recycling heat for greater efficiency. With a 12kg wash capacity and 8kg drying capacity, the large drum handles bigger loads while the standard-size design fits naturally into the home. The 5i brings intelligence through AI Super Wash & Dry. Its 13 sensors monitor factors including load weight, water hardness and temperature, automatically adjusting the cycle to suit each load. Its 4A energy efficiency can also help reduce the energy cost of everyday laundry. This thinking extends to Hisense's AI Companion Laundry Suite, introduced at IFA 2026. By recognizing clothing characteristics, the suite automatically selects suitable wash and dry cycles and adjusts the process, accordingly, creating a more seamless load-and-go experience. For Hisense, intelligent technology should work quietly in the background, making everyday routines simpler and giving people more time for the moments that make life brighter. About Hisense Hisense, founded in 1969, is a globally recognized leader in home appliances and consumer electronics with operations in over 180 countries, specializing in delivering high-quality multimedia products, home appliances, and intelligent IT solutions. According to Omdia, Hisense ranks No. 1 globally in the 100-inch and over TV segment (2023-2026H1). As The Origin of RGB MiniLED, Hisense continues to lead the next-generation RGB MiniLED innovation. As an Official Partner of UEFA EURO 2028, Hisense continues its legacy of global sports partnerships, bringing people closer to the moments that unite fans around the world.

iq.title: مركز أبحاث: الإسلام قد يصبح أكبر ديانة في العالم بحلول عام 2035
iq.description: شفق نيوز- متابعة توقع مركز بيو للأبحاث، أن يتجاوز الإسلام المسيحية ليصبح أكبر ديانة في العالم بحلول عام 2035، مدفوعاً بارتفاع معدلات الخصوبة لدى المسلمين، واستمرار نمو أعداد أتباعه بوتيرة أسرع من أتباع الديانات الأخرى. وأظهرت دراسة للمركز أن عدد المسلمين مرشح للارتفاع إلى نحو 2.57 مليار نسمة بحلول عام 2035، مقابل 2.52 مليار مسيحي، في تحول ينهي تصدر المسيحية قائمة أكبر الديانات في العالم، بعد احتفاظها بهذا الموقع لقرون. ووفقاً للتوقعات، إذا استمرت الاتجاهات الحالية، سيصل عدد المسلمين بحلول عام 2070 إلى نحو 3.6 مليار نسمة، مقابل ثلاثة مليارات مسيحي، لترتفع حصة المسلمين من سكان العالم إلى 37 بالمئة، مقارنة بـ26 بالمئة عام 2020، فيما ستبقى نسبة المسيحيين عند نحو 29 بالمئة، ليحتلوا المرتبة الثانية عالمياً. وعزت الدراسة هذا النمو بصورة رئيسية إلى ارتفاع معدلات الخصوبة، إذ يبلغ متوسط عدد الأطفال لكل امرأة مسلمة 3.1 طفل، مقابل 2.5 طفل لكل امرأة مسيحية خلال الفترة بين عامي 2020 و2025. وفي المقابل، بلغ متوسط الخصوبة لدى بقية الفئات الدينية مجتمعة 1.6 طفل لكل امرأة، وهو أقل من معدل الإحلال السكاني البالغ 2.1 طفل، الذي يُعد ضرورياً للحفاظ على حجم السكان عبر الأجيال. وذكر مركز بيو، وهو مؤسسة أبحاث مستقلة مقرها واشنطن، أن النمو السكاني الطبيعي، الناتج عن زيادة المواليد على الوفيات، يمثل العامل الأكبر في تغير التركيبة الدينية للسكان، إلى جانب التحول من دين إلى آخر. وبحسب الدراسة، من المتوقع أن يخسر الإسلام والمسيحية أتباعاً نتيجة التحول إلى ديانات أخرى أو التخلي عن الانتماء الديني، إلا أن حجم الخسائر سيكون متفاوتاً؛ إذ يُرجح أن يفقد الإسلام نحو ثمانية ملايين شخص بين عامي 2020 و2070، مقابل 105 ملايين للمسيحية. وتشير التوقعات إلى أن سكان العالم سيزدادون بنسبة 29 بالمئة خلال الفترة ذاتها، فيما سيكون الإسلام والمسيحية المجموعتين الدينيتين الوحيدتين اللتين ستواكبان هذا المعدل أو تتجاوزانه، مع نمو متوقع يبلغ 80 بالمئة للإسلام و30 بالمئة للمسيحية. أما الهندوس، فمن المتوقع أن يرتفع عددهم الإجمالي، لكن نسبتهم من سكان العالم ستنخفض قليلاً لتبلغ 13.6 بالمئة بحلول عام 2070، فيما يُتوقع أن يسجل اليهود نمطاً مشابهاً، مع وصول نسبتهم إلى 0.17 بالمئة. وفي المقابل، يُرجح أن يتراجع عدد البوذيين ونسبتهم من سكان العالم إلى نحو 2.5 بالمئة، بينما ستشهد الديانات الأخرى، بما فيها البهائية والطاوية والجاينية والسيخية والديانات المحلية، زيادة طفيفة في أعداد أتباعها، مع انخفاض حصتها الإجمالية إلى أقل من اثنين بالمئة من سكان العالم. وتوقعت الدراسة أيضاً تراجع نسبة الأشخاص الذين لا ينتمون إلى أي دين، بمن فيهم الملحدون واللاأدريون، من 24 بالمئة من سكان العالم عام 2020 إلى 17 بالمئة بحلول عام 2070. ولفتت إلى أن التغيرات لن تقتصر على أعداد أتباع الديانات ونسبهم، بل ستمتد إلى توزيعهم الجغرافي؛ إذ من المتوقع أن تبقى المسيحية أكبر ديانة في الولايات المتحدة بحلول عام 2070، لكنها لن تمثل غالبية السكان. كما يُرجح أن تتجاوز جمهورية الكونغو الديمقراطية الولايات المتحدة لتصبح الدولة التي تضم أكبر عدد من المسيحيين في العالم.

za.title: Leading South African Sport Mega-Event Legacy Scholar Professor Urmilla Bob Joins African Collaborations Group (ACG) Research & Impact Advisory Panel to Strengthen the Evidence Base for Sport and Entertainment Districts Across Africa
za.description: African Collaborations Group (ACG) (www.ACGafrica.com), the leading strategic project origination and collaboration platform focused on the industrialisation of sport in Africa through the origination of bankable sport and entertainment district ecosystems, today announced the appointment of Professor Urmilla Bob to its Research&Impact Advisory Panel. Professor Bob is Professor of Geography and Environmental Sciences at the University of KwaZulu-Natal (UKZN) in South Africa, one of the continent’s most respected research-intensive universities. She is one of Africa’s foremost authorities on the legacy of sport mega-events and sport infrastructure investments in developing nations. Over a career spanning more than 15 years in sport-related research, Professor Bob has produced a body of work that is directly relevant to the challenge ACG was created to address. Her research systematically examines what happens after the event is over: whether the economic projections materialise, whether the infrastructure delivers lasting value, whether communities benefit, and whether the social legacies promised by host governments are realised. Her findings have consistently demonstrated that sport infrastructure investments in developing countries frequently fall short of their projected returns, with benefits unevenly distributed and legacy planning often inadequate. This body of evidence is foundational to ACG’s entire model. The Victory District™ concept was conceived precisely because the approach Professor Bob has documented, standalone stadiums built for a single event with insufficient legacy planning, has repeatedly failed to deliver lasting value. ACG’s integrated district model is designed to address the structural shortcomings her research has identified: by embedding sport venues within a financially self-sustaining, mixed-use ecosystem that generates revenue, employment, and community value 365 days a year. Professor Bob’s research on the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa is among the most cited work globally on sport mega-event legacy in the developing world. Her publications, including “Sport Mega-Events and Their Legacies: The 2010 FIFA World Cup” (co-authored with Scarlett Cornelissen and Kamilla Swart), “Sport Events and Social Legacies,” and her work developing indicator frameworks for assessing legacy impacts, have shaped how scholars, policymakers, and international institutions understand the long-term consequences of sport infrastructure investment in Africa. Beyond mega-event legacy, Professor Bob has co-authored vital frameworks and studies on the development of national sport tourism strategies in South Africa, analysing how leisure patterns, economic activity, and media coverage shift before, during, and after major events. This sport tourism expertise is directly relevant to the hospitality and tourism components within Victory District™ projects, where visitor spend, event-driven travel, and year-round programming are critical to financial sustainability. Professor Bob is a Senior and Principal Researcher for the South African Cultural Observatory (SACO), funded by South Africa’s national Department of Sport, Arts and Culture to provide research and training support. She has led and continues to be involved in numerous sport-related research projects for the Department. This direct relationship with the South African government’s sport and culture ministry, combined with her deep expertise in the African sport infrastructure landscape, gives ACG’s Research&Impact Advisory Panel something no non-African scholar can provide: a senior African academic voice that has studied sport infrastructure legacy on the continent, in the cities where the infrastructure was built, over more than a decade. “Professor Bob has spent her career answering the question that every government asks before investing in sport infrastructure: will it deliver lasting value?” said Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard (www. Pompigne-Mognard.com), Founder and Executive Chairman of ACG. “Her research has shown, with rigorous evidence, that the traditional approach too often falls short. ACG’s Victory District™ model was designed to change that outcome. Having the scholar who documented the failures now helping to validate the solution gives ACG an unparalleled level of academic credibility on the African continent. za.title: AI leadership: 3 success lessons from CBA’s chief AI officer
za.description: These are early, fascinating days for the corporate title du jour — chief artificial intelligence officer (CAIO). So when the CAIO of Australia’s largest bank, Commonwealth Bank (CBA), stands up to talk about his role and how times are changing, it’s worth a closer look. I recently interviewed Ranil Boteju, CBA’s CAIO, on stage at Momentum Media’s FST Future of Financial Services, Data & AI conference, and one of his answers pointed to the story behind the story. “I am the chief AI officer, but I’m one of many.” The real chief AI officer, he said, is “our CEO.” Every organization is different, but it points to an early dilemma for CAIOs. Who, exactly, should be in charge of this AI transformation movement? CFOs, CMOs, CIOs and even CISOs have a stake, and the benefit is well-documented roles with clear areas of responsibility. And of course, as Boteju notes, the CEO is key. If CEOs don’t ‘get it,’ the organization has bigger problems. Mark Jones, The Story Code Co. CAIOs finding their feet Keep that tension in mind because Boteju’s experience offers plenty of lessons for companies forging an AI transformation path. CAIOs occupy a rare space in the race to AI adoption: they’re highly influential and respected yet hold varying degrees of authority. Boteju does run a centre of excellence and builds the shared capabilities the business draws on, but if we step back, he still has a structural problem. Like chief digital officers before him — a parallel he drew himself — Boteju holds a role that champions a technology which creates value only when it’s embedded across the entire business. “The chief digital officer was a digital team, and they were doing digital, and everyone was by definition not digital,” he said. The lesson he took from that era is noteworthy: “AI transformation can’t be constrained to one team.” Clearly he’s not responsible for a vertical silo like his C-suite peers and, I’d add, necessarily so. Each business unit should “really lead their agenda”, he said, underpinned by “a common set of capabilities that I would build”. CAIOs must master managing up to their CEO, collaborating sideways across the C-suite and providing the top-down inspiration that helps whole teams embrace and extend the vision for AI transformation. So, what’s his story? All this is vital because it shapes how leaders should understand his story. I picked up three lessons from his talk and our conversation. 1. Context is your moat Before your buzzword filter goes off, this insight is worth a closer look. When everyone has relatively equal access to the same AI technologies, or at least the same large language models, it pays to understand how your competitive moat is changing. “In a world where all of the banks are using the same models, what will differentiate us is the context, the organizational memory, all of the tacit knowledge that sits in people’s heads,” Boteju said. “This is effectively our moat.” That’s the scarce, underused asset inside most companies: what your people know but have never written down. The patterns they’ve recognized over time, and their hard-earned wisdom. A standard operating process, he noted, “is pretty high-level. A lot of it sits in people’s heads.” Of course, some of this knowledge can also be found scattered throughout vast collections of unstructured data in all organizations. But his point is that analysis isn’t the gap. Asked when data is good enough, he said that in most financial services organizations “there is no excuse to wait”. So, here’s the better question: how much of what your organization knows has been written down, and how much of it could you hand to an agent tomorrow? 2. Simplify your strategy Oh, how we love to overcomplicate enterprise IT strategies! And yet Boteju stood on stage with clean, simple slides that broke down his strategic thinking. “The reason for doing AI needs to be really clear in your organization,” he said. “We’re not jumping on a bandwagon.” CBA has chosen four strategic priorities: customer experience, fraud and scams, faster delivery and reimagining work. Each one makes sense, so that begs the next question: how can AI deliver against each of these easily understood priorities at scale? The answer for CBA is five enablers, also presented on one slide: one AI platform, an AI control plane, token optimization, context and knowledge, and skills and capabilities. The alternative is a familiar story to anyone in this game. A few years ago, he said, it was “1,000 flowers blooming, lots of duplication, lots of POCs, nothing really scaled.” His advice now is to have “a really narrow set of … use cases to focus on”. Could you put your AI strategy on one page? 3. AI transformation is a control game This point is a meta-insight I took from CBA’s big picture. Think about the dominant AI industry narrative pushed by the LLM leaders in particular: you can’t control AI — heck, even we can’t control agents and we built them! Now contrast that with Boteju’s approach, which he describes as “machine layers of defence”. “We register every single asset,” he said. “Any given moment, I can point to all of the AI agents that are underway, live in production or being built.” Nothing goes live unless it passes pre-deployment testing. Then, in his words: “Has there been any drift? Is there anything that we need to be concerned about? We can monitor that in real time.” Outcomes are checked after the fact, and an independent team validates the lot. Know what you can control and what you can’t — and have a plan for both. And look back at the five enablers for a moment. Maintaining control is a strategy that runs through most of them: the AI platform and control plane, token spend (a single gateway, caps for engineers and smaller, cheaper models for less intensive tasks), and how context is protected. “To pick out the one thing at the bank that we need to really protect,” he said, “it’s our context and knowledge.” The final enabler is a handy $90m, which he said CBA is investing in upskilling teams. In short, this is the behaviour of an organization that’s not lying down and letting the AI juggernaut run over it. What’s your story? It’s often said, “comparison is the thief of joy” — but in this case it should be an opportunity for inspiration and pointed reflection. What comes to mind when you look at CBA’s approach and then hold up a mirror? You might have a CAIO who’s been given all the responsibility and none of the authority. Or perhaps your organization lacks the clarity of strategic thinking clearly evident at CBA? As always, success is not contingent on one C-suite title, but on how your entire team understands and communicates the story of change that’s required in times like these. Times when new titles come and go, change feels faster than ever, and clarity can feel like a distant dream enjoyed by others. In my mind, it starts with challenging the control narrative. Are you living inside your own story, or the AI industry’s adopted fear, uncertainty and doubt (FUD) narrative?
